Almost every LinkedIn video hands you a list of posting tips and stops there. This one follows the actual path a buyer takes before they ever send a DM: a comment in someone else's feed, a profile click, a post reaching them weeks later. For founders, consultants, and operators posting without pipeline, seeing LinkedIn from the buyer's side is what makes the platform stop feeling random.

This video covers the full LinkedIn client journey for 2026: the Authority Paradox that keeps experts invisible, the comment system that borrows other creators' audiences, Total Addressable Content, and the March 2026 feed rebuild that moved LinkedIn to a single LLM-powered ranking model scoring posts by percentile and favoring smaller accounts. 

It breaks down the five formats that put your expertise into conversations already happening (brandjacking, newsjacking, memejacking, hot takes, and the trend rider), the 50 word algorithm audition your hook has to pass, and the four bucket content funnel of 40% growth, 30% authority, 20% conversion, 10% personal.

Real proof runs through it: a Distinctiva client who went from 800K to 3.6 million ARR with over 80% of pipeline from LinkedIn and zero outbound, an SEO consultant who changed only his headline and About section and saw reach climb 226% and engagement 327%, and a memejacking post that got Stephen Bartlett to comment for 147,000 impressions.

WHAT YOU'LL LEARN:
 Why your next client meets you in someone else's comment section first
 The Authority Paradox: why deep expertise and attention are two different currencies
 How to build a 20 to 30 creator list whose audience is full of your buyers
 Why your profile is the landing page your content points at
 What LinkedIn's March 2026 feed rebuild changed and why it favors smaller accounts
 Total Addressable Content and the five formats that borrow reach you haven't earned yet
 The 50 word algorithm audition every post has to pass before a human sees it
 Why you should write your hook last, and the four bucket funnel that turns readers into pipeline

KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 Expertise and attention are different currencies, and on LinkedIn you build attention on purpose
 Your first touch with a future client usually happens in the comments of someone they already follow
 Every comment you leave carries your headline into rooms you're not in
 LinkedIn's March 2026 feed converts engagement into percentiles, which made its content matching 30 times more accurate
 The rebuilt algorithm gave a reach lift to members with fewer connections, so smaller accounts have a structural edge
 One Distinctiva client hit 3.6 million ARR with over 80% of pipeline from LinkedIn and zero outbound
